video_directives: Vary shot lengths more: the mid-section door-pose beats (9-16s) hold near-identical compositions too long; tighten each pose to ~1.2-1.5s
Push secondary animation: side characters and NPCs react well in wide shots but freeze in close-ups; keep idle sway/blink alive under every zoom
Motivate transitions with motion: add directional camera pushes tied to the character's pointing/box-reveal gestures so cuts feel caused, not just sequenced

top3_directives: Cut header to ≤5 words (e.g. 'EVERYONE HAS A PRICE') — currently 7 words + two price tags = 9 visible, breaching the 8-word ceiling
Unify the two text systems: integrate the $50,000 tag into the same visual language as the $0 tag (same tag style/orientation) so it reads as one system, not header + floating labels
Ground the glow: the hero character's orange rim-light spills onto nothing at the feet — add a soft contact shadow consistent with the supporting cast's shadows for cohesion
Third character on right edge is cropped awkwardly with a stray third face — either fully frame or remove it
$2,500 and $50,000 labels are nearly identical weight; differentiate the target ($50,000) with stronger emphasis so the eye path reads goal vs. current
Large empty upper-left quadrant (purple sky) is a dead zone — add subtle depth cue or shift composition to reduce it
Fill the bottom ~25% dead zone with grounded detail (street texture, reflections, foreground silhouette) or raise character placement
The tan window panel and metal door crop awkwardly mid-frame — either pull them fully into frame or push them to clean partial bleeds
Add subtle rim-light direction consistency: the warm glow on the character conflicts with cool red ambient; tint shadow side to unify palette
Fill or compress the large empty ellipse/dead zone between the title and the characters — the middle third of the frame carries no visual information
Unify the header and price-tag text styles (corner radius, stroke weight) so the two text systems read as one coherent UI language
Push background building silhouettes slightly darker/desaturated to increase separation for the glowing character cutouts on 6-inch daylight screens
Top third is a soft dead zone — push the red orbital ring/moon higher contrast or drop a subtle vignette to tie it to the subject
The fallen doors on the right read slightly muddy against the background panels; add a rim shadow or 5-8% value separation
Give the $0 badge a drop shadow or glow stroke so it detaches from the dark skyline behind it
The '$0' sign slightly overlaps the red orbit ring behind it — give it a drop shadow or backing glow to fully separate it from the ring line
Lower third is a large dead zone (dark floor from ~1500-1900px) — add a subtle floor reflection or vignette-driven glow so the bottom doesn't go pitch black on phone screens
Character's orange rim glow is uneven (strong on left, thin on right) — balance the backlight so the silhouette reads equally from both edges
Resolve the awkward left-edge crop of the door frame — either fully crop it out or pull it fully into frame
Deepen the background silhouette contrast slightly so city shapes read as depth layers instead of mid-tone mush
Consider a subtle ground shadow/anchor under the character's feet for stronger spatial grounding
Upper 40% of frame is a near-empty dead zone — push the skyline/moon composition up or lower the action to close the gap
The $50,000 tag is the only hierarchy anchor; add a subtle glow or scale bump so the eye finds it before the busy door cluster
Foreground doors on the left edge are cropped into ambiguous dark shapes — raise their rim-light separation from the background buildings
Trim the oversized red orbit ring — it passes awkwardly behind the $0 tag and reads as a stray line at the frame edges
Reposition the $8,000 tag so its pointer doesn't collide with the cropped hooded NPC; either fully frame that character or push it further off-screen
Deepen the bottom-quarter foreground shadow slightly to give the glowing figure a stronger grounded contact shadow and reduce the dead pavement zone
Add a subtle rim/glow edge to the '$0' sign so it separates from the dark navy background like the character does
Fill the bottom-third dead zone: the character's lower body runs off-frame into empty dark space — extend floor reflection or streetlight detail
The cropped right arm exits frame awkwardly mid-forearm — either pull it fully in-frame or crop at a cleaner joint
Replace the flat red band behind the dollar figure with a gradient or slight drop shadow so the banner reads as a designed plate, not a raw rectangle
Fill the bottom-third dead zone (dark empty street below the character) with subtle reflections or foreground silhouettes to extend depth
Unify the palette: the warm red upper zone and cool purple lower zone meet abruptly — blend with a transition glow or grade one hue family across the frame
Separate the dark hooded figures overlapping the children characters — the occlusion creates mushy silhouettes and hides key shapes on both sides
Rebalance focal competition: the two price tags pull equally against the glowing central figure — dim the tags or visually link each tag to its owner with a connector/pointer
Raise separation between foreground characters and the dark midground buildings — the black figures melt into the dark-purple background on small screens
